review_method: AI-assisted independent read-only cross-batch review; no human or ecclesiastical review claimed.

notes.finding: No semantic identity collision found after reading baseline names and alternate names. Similar names remain different people: Gertrude of Nivelles / Gertrude the Great; Mechthild of Hackeborn / Matilda of Ringelheim; Anselm of Lucca / Anselm of Canterbury; Hugh of Cluny / Hugh of Grenoble; Odo of Cluny / Odilo of Cluny; Caesarius of Arles / Caesarius of Nazianzus; Stephen of Hungary / Stephen the first martyr; Henry II / Henry Morse or Henry Walpole.

All 60 historical original biographies were read against their cached main Catholic institutional source texts. Their core life facts are supported. Dates, reported miracles, reader-supplied additions and conflicting chronology are generally qualified or omitted. The writing agent subsequently moved several methodological limitations out of biographies into uncertainty_note; these moves do not alter the assessed core facts.

notes.source_reader_evidence: Primary Catholic Benedictine abbey source opened through web reader from the Nominis link. Its Saints of Minster section, lines 79–81 in the reader result, was read.
notes.finding: The abbey identifies St. Mildred as its second abbess, describes ongoing veneration of her relics in its chapel and a local feast. This provides independent institutional recognition of traditional Catholic veneration without inventing a modern canonization or Roman Martyrology notice.
notes.limitation: Its death year 725 differs from the Nominis heading 700, so retaining null dates is appropriate. Source addition and improved recognition wording suggested to owning agent; no historical batch was edited by this reviewer.

notes.finding: The source pages are titled Saint and include a Martyrologe romain signature and commemoration information, but their cached text lacks a separate standard notice explicitly naming the saint. The statement that a reproduced notice separately names this individual should be qualified. This is an evidence-description issue rather than a discovery that either person is unrecognized.
notes.reported_to: Owning historical agent and root; no direct edits made.
